title: Chorus component orchestration and fluid rhythm system for console panels
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console panels (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) currently use a mix of ad-hoc spacing, animation timing, and microcomponent states across teams. This causes visual drift, unstable perceived performance, and a heavy maintenance burden for Figma libraries and dev handoffs.

Goal: Define a lightweight orchestration layer called 'Chorus' for panel components that codifies rhythm (spacing and timing), state choreography (hover / focussed / streaming / loading / error), and token mappings for color/typography/motion. The Chorus system should be: 1) easy to adopt in new and legacy panels, 2) produce predictable animation timing for streaming tokens and rollout transitions, 3) map to an exportable Figma library and a small set of CSS/Token variables for frontend engineers.

Scope: global spacing rhythm, motion durations, microinteraction easing presets, component state choreography for cards/rails/modals, token naming recommendations, and Figma library organization. Not in scope: full redesign of individual cards or data-model changes for cost calculations.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Figma library with Chorus tokens (spacing X, rhythm Y, motion Z) and 6 example components (metric card, cost sparkline, rollout rail, compact table row, error sheet, streaming chip). 2) Implementation-ready token mapping doc (token names, hex/px/ms values, usage guidance). 3) Accessibility checklist for motion reduction, contrast, and focus order. 4) Two engineering reviews completed and a GH PR with a small CSS token shim prototype. 5) Design review approved by PM and Accessibility lead.

Notes: emphasize minimal runtime surface area for engineers (<= 12 tokens initially). Provide migration guide for legacy components with examples of phased rollouts (canary component variant).
